Hi Anna — thanks for sending this over. Quick checklist from our side so we can move to payment: 

1) Tax form: since you indicated Astoria is a US entity we need a completed, signed W-9 (name on W-9 should match the legal payee name you want on the vendor profile). If you are claiming exemption for 1099, please mark that on the W-9 and provide the legal justification.

2) Legal entity verification: please attach one of the following (preferably the first two):
   - Articles of incorporation / formation (PDF)
   - Recent IRS EIN verification letter (CP 575) or a screenshot of EIN confirmation
   - A recent bank statement with the legal name (if incorporation docs not available)

3) Payment routing: ACH is ok. We need: account name, account number, routing number, and whether the account is in the payee name. For wire: bank name, SWIFT, account IBAN (if applicable). Please do not send full bank PDFs by email if you can avoid it — a redacted PDF or the bank-detail stub is fine.

4) PO / remit reference: include PO-9981 and invoice 4432 on the remittance line. That helps auto-match.

If you can send the signed W-9 + one verification doc and a bank stub, I will route to AP (Marcus) for vendor creation and payment scheduling.

Action items: Anna to provide signed W-9 + EIN proof + bank stub. Marcus will confirm setup timeline once docs are received.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Looping in AP details — Priya, thanks for the checklist. A couple of internal notes / asks to keep this smooth: 

- If the expected payment amount is > $250k over a rolling 12-month window we request a beneficial ownership attestation. Can you confirm total expected 2026 spend?
- For vendor setup we need a scanned signature on the W-9 (acceptable), plus one ID for the signer if the signatory is not listed on formation docs.
- Timeline: once we receive the signed W-9 + EIN proof + bank stub, AP turnaround for first payment is typically 7-10 business days (assuming no tax issues). If they want faster funding we can process a wire but that needs CFO approval and a wire fee.

Also, please ask Astoria to confirm whether they are a disregarded entity/sole proprietor vs C-Corp/S-Corp/LLC taxed as corp — this affects 1099 classification. If they are incorporated (C or S corp) they are generally exempt from 1099-MISC/NEC, but we still keep the W-9 on file.

Marcus Lin
